hints: The swimming times are normally distributed with mean $\mu = 62$ seconds and standard deviation $\sigma = 5$ seconds: $X \sim \mathrm{N}(62, 5^2)$.
Express the interval probability in terms of $\Phi(z)$: $\mathrm{P}(-1.2 < Z < 0.8) = \Phi(0.8) - \Phi(-1.2) = \Phi(0.8) - [1 - \Phi(1.2)]$.
walkthrough:
Standardise the boundaries $56$ and $66$ using $\mu = 62$ and $\sigma = 5$:
$$Z_1 = \dfrac{56 - 62}{5} = -1.2, \quad Z_2 = \dfrac{66 - 62}{5} = 0.8$$

Write the probability in terms of the standard normal distribution function:
$$\mathrm{P}(56 < X < 66) = \mathrm{P}(-1.2 < Z < 0.8) = \Phi(0.8) - \Phi(-1.2)$$

Look up cumulative probabilities from the normal table and evaluate:
$$\Phi(0.8) = 0.7881, \quad \Phi(1.2) = 0.8849$$
$$\mathrm{P}(56 < X < 66) = 0.7881 - (1 - 0.8849) = 0.7881 - 0.1151 = 0.673$$
teacher_walkthrough: Let $X$ denote the time in seconds taken by a randomly chosen club member to swim 100 metres.

Step 2: Express the interval in terms of the standard normal cdf $\Phi$:
$$\mathrm{P}(-1.2 < Z < 0.8) = \Phi(0.8) - \Phi(-1.2)$$

Step 3: Use the symmetry property $\Phi(-z) = 1 - \Phi(z)$ for the negative value:
$$\Phi(-1.2) = 1 - \Phi(1.2)$$
So the expression becomes:
$$\Phi(0.8) - [1 - \Phi(1.2)] = \Phi(0.8) + \Phi(1.2) - 1$$

Step 4: Look up values from the Cambridge MF19 normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.8) = 0.7881$$
$$\Phi(1.2) = 0.8849$$

Step 5: Compute the numerical result:
$$\mathrm{P}(56 < X < 66) = 0.7881 - (1 - 0.8849) = 0.7881 - 0.1151 = 0.6730$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $0.673$.

hints: Notice the units: $t$ is given in minutes, while the normal distribution is defined in seconds. So $t$ minutes equals $60t$ seconds.
13% take more than $t$ minutes, which means $\mathrm{P}(X > 60t) = 0.13$, so the area below $60t$ is $1 - 0.13 = 0.87$.
Find the critical value $z$ where $\Phi(z) = 0.87$: from tables, $z = 1.127$.
Set up the standardisation equation $\dfrac{60t - 62}{5} = 1.127$, solve for $60t$, and divide by 60 to find $t$ in minutes.
walkthrough:
Convert the cutoff time $t$ minutes into seconds: $\text{Time in seconds} = 60t$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 60t) = 0.13 \implies \mathrm{P}(X < 60t) = 0.87$$

Find the $z$-value corresponding to a cumulative probability of $0.87$:
$$\Phi(z) = 0.87 \implies z = 1.127$$
teacher_walkthrough: We are told that 13% of the members of the club take more than $t$ minutes to swim 100 metres.

Step 1: Be careful with the units.
The swimming model has mean $\mu = 62$ seconds and standard deviation $\sigma = 5$ seconds.
The unknown $t$ is expressed in minutes.
Therefore, the cutoff time in seconds is $60t$.

Step 2: Relate the percentage to the standard normal distribution.
13% take more than $60t$ seconds:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 60t) = 0.13$$
Using the complement rule:
$$\mathrm{P}(X < 60t) = 1 - 0.13 = 0.87$$
$$\Phi(z) = 0.87$$

Step 3: Look up $z$ in the normal distribution table:
In the main table, $\Phi(1.12) = 0.8686$.
We need $0.8700 - 0.8686 = 0.0014 = 14$ in the differences table.
In row $1.12$, a difference of 14 corresponds to 7.
Thus, $z = 1.127$.

Step 4: Set up the standardisation equation:
$$\frac{60t - 62}{5} = 1.127$$

Step 5: Solve for $t$:
$$60t - 62 = 5 \times 1.127 = 5.635$$
$$60t = 62 + 5.635 = 67.635$$
$$t = \frac{67.635}{60} = 1.12725$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $t = 1.13$ minutes.
